rationale: The two established findings are unchanged; this update firms up a boundary of the trim finding. Its account states that snapshot-based compaction remains available under the same configuration and that this was source-derived rather than measured, so I added a snapshot measurement to every case of the trim probe and validated it locally: after the two trim calls, `snapshot(Some(decided_idx), true)` returns ok and moves the compacted index from 0 to 1 in {1,2,5}, {2,3,4} and the two-node {1,3}, i.e. the alternative compaction path works exactly where trim cannot, while in the contiguous control it is a no-op because trim already compacted that index. The extended probe is submitted as the successor execution with three added comparisons (predicted holds, applicable only where the trim path made no progress). I also read the entry-deriving macro crate this turn and found no lead worth pursuing there.

investigations.discriminator: Pending: the snapshot boundary measurement submitted here, which should confirm that the alternative compaction path still compacts under the defect's trigger. After that the question is settled for four id sets and four trim observations; only same-cause variants remain.

experiment.revision_reason: Added one boundary measurement per case and three comparisons for it: after `trim(None)` and `trim(Some(decided_idx_before_trim))`, each case calls `snapshot(Some(decided_idx_before_trim), true)` on the same leader and reports whether the compacted index advanced. Cases A {1,2,3}, B {1,2,5}, C {2,3,4} and D {1,3}, their scenario, their trim measurements and their four comparisons are unchanged. The new comparisons assert that the snapshot path advances compaction, and are declared applicable only where the trim path left the compacted index at 0.

scope.description: Four runs of one cluster shape with real `OmniPaxos` instances driven directly through the public API in a single process (lossless in-process delivery, one entry appended on the elected leader and decided by every configured server). Each run calls `trim(None)`, then `trim(Some(decided_idx_before_trim))`, then `snapshot(Some(decided_idx_before_trim), true)`, sampling `get_compacted_idx()` after each call. Case A is the contiguous control {1,2,3}; B, C and D are the trigger configurations {1,2,5}, {2,3,4} (leader 2, id 1 absent) and the two-node {1,3}.
assumptions: Node ids need not be contiguous or start at 1: `ClusterConfig::validate` requires only more than one node, a non-zero configuration id, a valid quorum and that the node set contains this server's pid.

The entry type's `Snapshot::create` is implemented for the probe so the snapshot call exercises the real `try_snapshot` path (trim, compacted index and snapshot write) rather than panicking on a placeholder type.
In-process lossless delivery preserves the properties needed: every configured server decides the entry before the compaction calls.
The first id of each set carries leader_priority 1 so elections are deterministic and only the id set differs.
excluded: Any claim about clusters larger than four nodes or id sets beyond these four.
Any claim about snapshot merging across restarts or about `local_only = false` forwarding.
Any safety claim: this probe measures progress of two compaction paths.

experiment.prefix: For each case: build one `OmniPaxos<TestEntry, MemoryStorage<TestEntry>>` per node id (configuration_id 1, election_tick_timeout 3, resend_message_tick_timeout 5, batch_size 1, first id leader_priority 1), elect the first id by calling `try_become_leader()` and pumping (tick every instance, take_outgoing_messages, deliver each message to its receiver's handle_incoming) until the second id reports it as accepted leader, emit the admission event, append one entry on the leader and pump until every configured server reports decided index >= 1, then call `trim(None)`, `trim(Some(decided_idx_before_trim))` and `snapshot(Some(decided_idx_before_trim), true)` in that order, sampling the compacted index after each. Emit the outcome under the mode-specific event name with the node list, leader, decided index, both trim results, both trim compaction outcomes, the snapshot result and whether it advanced compaction.
experiment.responsibility: The decisive inputs come from the target: `LeaderState`'s id-sized accepted-index vector and `get_min_all_accepted_idx` fix the trim index at 0, so `try_trim` cannot advance, while `try_snapshot` derives its target from the decided index and therefore still writes a snapshot and advances the compacted index. The caller supplies only the optional indices.

comparisons.description: Control: trim(None) advances compaction when the largest id equals the node count.
Ids {2,3,4} with id 1 absent: expected violated.
Boundary on {1,2,5}: the snapshot path still advances compaction where trim cannot. Expected holds.
Boundary on the two-node {1,3}. Expected holds.

semantic_changes: One measurement (a snapshot call after the two trim calls) and three boundary comparisons added per case; existing scenarios, measurements and comparisons unchanged.
